dedupe_keys.name: booss building object and outdoor scene segmentation multi channel rgb and thermal aerial imagery datasets

description: BOOSS is a set of aerial images in visible (RGB) and thermal infrared channels with pixel-level labels of building components and outdoor scene objects, for training semantic segmentation models. It was produced by Yu Hou and Lucio Soibelman of the University of Southern California with Rebekka Volk of the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, and accompanies the 2021 Remote Sensing paper 'An Approach to Semantically Segmenting Building Components and Outdoor Scenes Based on Multichannel Aerial Imagery Datasets'. Version 1.0 labels roofs, facades, cars, roof equipment and ground equipment, with ground truth, RGB and thermal images supplied side by side. Access: one zip file of about 0.9 GB, openly downloadable from Zenodo since 1 August 2021. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10.3390/rs13214357) is CC-BY-4.0. Access is free of charge. Coverage: drone-collected scenes described in the paper; the record does not list the sites. Caveats: a small research benchmark with few classes. Simulation uses are automated thermal inspection of building envelopes to locate heat loss for retrofit planning, and component-level inputs for building digital twins. Related records: the BIO LoD3 building point cloud benchmark and the Duke aerial imagery dataset.
